questions.topic: LOGIC: fuse input jumper lugs 1.86 mm apart
questions.text: On each LOGIC bus strip, a jumper lug's ring sits 1.86 mm from the neck of the lug next to it (both on the SAME strip, so the same circuit: all Bus 1 or all Bus 2). With the same parts this cannot reach 3 mm: the fuses are 8.1 mm apart and the 1 in strip is too short for a higher second row. Bus 1 to Bus 2 is fixed (3.18 mm, was 0.68). Until you answer, the new 3 mm gate lets only this one gap through.

options.label: Keep it: the 3 mm rule is between different circuits; lugs on one strip are one circuit
Spread the fuses to a 9.3 mm pitch: LOGIC box about 15 mm deeper
Taller strips (1.5 in bar, a new part) and a higher second lug row: LOGIC box about 16 mm taller

questions.topic: Live parts touching plastic or wire insulation
questions.text: These are live metal against plastic or insulation, not against another live part: a strip resting on its spine lips (0.4 mm, that is how it is held), the POWER belly pan under the lug bolts (0.59 mm), LOGIC jumper parts to the deck (0.6 mm). The wire simulation adds: 2 Bus 1 fuse wires pass 0.2-0.3 mm from the Bus 1 strip bolt heads, and 3 wires on the LOGIC outboard relay column rub the belly pan wall (those relay pins are 1 mm from the wall, same as rev 6).

options.label: Keep as is: plastic and insulation may touch live parts; the 3 mm rule stays live-to-live
Keep, but add rub protection: a printed rib between the Bus 1 wires and the strip bolt heads, and a relief in the pan wall at the outboard relay column
3 mm air to every plastic part and wire too (strips on standoffs, pan lower, boxes about 3 mm taller)

questions.topic: Two wires crimped in one terminal (overfilled)
questions.text: The harness puts two wires in one terminal at 3 places: LOGIC HL and HR fuse outputs (relay 30 + 86: 14 + 18 AWG = 2.9 mm2 in a TE 880398-2, max 2.5 mm2) and k_horn terminal 30 (16 + 18 AWG = 2.13 mm2 in a TE 42281-1, max 2.0 mm2).

options.label: One wire per terminal: one wire out of the box to a splice that feeds relay 30 and 86 (ST185-CabinPower change)
A bigger terminal that takes both wires (new part, cavity check)
Feed each relay's 86 from its own small fuse

questions.topic: LOGIC wires that go out and come back in
questions.text: 5 wires run from a Bus 1 fuse to a relay in the same LOGIC box (HL 30 + 86, HR 30 + 86, ETB 30). The two copper strips stand between them under the deck, so the simulation takes them out of the front exit, round, and back in. They fit (Bus 1 exit: 12 wires in its 8.8 mm notch), but the loop sits outside the box.

options.label: Keep the loops (tie them to the harness at the front)
Add a printed channel across the front of the strips so they stay inside the box

questions.topic: Route drawings 1, 7 and 11 still show the old fuse box (row 111)
questions.text: The fuse box moved, so 3 approved route drawings are out of date: Route 1 has no battery relay block in the trunk, Route 7 shows the old one-piece fuse box, and Route 11 runs the fuel pump feed from the glove box instead of from the trunk. (12 routes also use old fuse box names in their labels; an agent fixes those either way, labels only.) The rules say agents do not change a route without your markup (R47). How do these 3 get fixed?

options.label: An agent redraws them from the CAD and the approved harness drawings (relay block at the trunk battery corner, pump feed from it); you re-approve after
You mark up Routes 1, 7 and 11 first; then an agent redraws them
Leave the pictures; fix the labels and add a note that points to the fuse box CAD

questions.topic: The ECU 'engine stop' input has no switch (row 50)
questions.text: Your rules say two things stop the engine: the trunk kill switch AND the ECU's Stop Switch input (R19, R64). The kill switch is drawn and works on its own (it cuts the battery and the alternator), so the CSB3 being on a switched feed is fine. But the ECU stop input is not connected to anything, and all 10 ECU digital inputs are already used. What should trigger it?

options.label: A CSB3 button: a freed CSB3 input (S4 or S5) sends 'stop' to the ECU over CAN; no new ECU wire
Drop the ECU stop input; the trunk kill switch is the only stop (changes R19 / R64)
A separate dash switch wired to the ECU (an ECU pin has to be moved to free a digital input)

questions.text: The cluster shows KNOCK and beeps the moment the ECU's 0x3EE message says knock. That message goes out every 50 ms, so the warning can lag up to 50 ms. The RPM and boost messages already go every 10 ms. The bus has plenty of room and the cluster needs no change.

options.label: Yes, every 10 ms: an agent changes the 4 CAN files now and runs the parity check (R80)
No, keep 50 ms
20 ms as a middle step

questions.topic: When to build the circuit tracer (row 117)
questions.text: The circuit tracer (follows every circuit end to end, ECU on and off) was set to start once all drawings are final. All 15 are approved, but CabinPower will still change for the fuse box (row 113 and question J3).

options.label: After the fuse box is approved and the CabinPower follow-ups land (rows 107, 113)
Now, and run it again after CabinPower changes
Later; not needed before the build

questions.text: harness.design's Export > PDF only works by hand in the app. Our checker guesses the size of the title block and notes block in the corners until it sees one real export.

options.label: WheelSpeed-Rear now (small, final, will not change): export it and tell us if a corner block covers a note or wire
CabinPower, after its fuse box follow-ups land (row 113)
Wait until no drawing is changing any more

questions.topic: Route 8: ground stud for the cluster and RealDash Pi (row 70)
questions.text: The center cluster and the RealDash Pi each end in a ring for a cabin ground stud (M6), and their +12 V (DEV) comes from the glove box. Route 8 does not mark where that stud is.

options.label: The agent picks the nearest factory ground bolt behind the dash from the 1993 wiring book and draws it; you check it at the build
You mark the spot on Route 8
Use the same cabin ground stud as the alarm (Route 14)

questions.topic: VRC board holder: model it now? (row 97)
questions.text: The 3D-printed holder for the VRC board is not modelled yet. The board's size is known from the maker's published design files (about 24 x 24 mm), but your board is the DetonationEMS build and nobody has measured it.

options.label: Model it now from the published size with a little extra room; check the fit when the board is here (a reprint is cheap)
Wait until you measure the board

questions.topic: Right cluster rounding bug: fix the frozen firmware? (row 104)
questions.text: On the right cluster, lambda 0.9995-0.9999 shows '0.000' (right at the normal cruise value), and boost or timing with .95-.99 shows one number low (12.97 psi shows '12.0'). The fix is a small code change in the right-side cluster, which is frozen, so it needs your OK. The CAN audit found it only on the right cluster.

options.label: Yes: an agent fixes it in the right-side cluster repo; you reflash that cluster at the bench
No: keep the cluster frozen and live with it
Later, after the car runs

questions.topic: RealDash coolant pressure: when does it turn red? (row 32)
questions.text: Two of our docs disagree: the layout doc says red above 200 kPa, the build notes say 250 kPa. (The layout doc calls 50-150 kPa normal.)

options.label: 200 kPa, as the layout doc says: an agent fixes the build notes; the tile is checked on the Pi
250 kPa
Decide at the bench with the real sensor

questions.text: GitHub has a rule that asks Copilot to review every PR, but no review ever comes (your Copilot plan's monthly quota does not cover it). Nothing waits for it: PRs merge without it.

options.label: Leave it as is and close the item
Turn the rule off (you do it in the GitHub settings)
Check or upgrade the Copilot plan so reviews arrive
